passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: Loss Contingencies We are currently involved in various claims and legal proceedings. We regularly review the status of each significant matter and assess its potential financial exposure. If the potential loss from any claim or legal proceeding is considered probable and the amount can be reasonably estimated, we accrue a liability for the estimated loss. Significant judgment is required in both the determination of probability and whether an exposure is reasonably estimable. Our judgments are subjective based on the status of the legal or regulatory proceedings, the merits of our defenses and consultation with in-house and outside legal counsel. Because of uncertainties related to these matters, accruals are based only on the best information available at the time. As additional information becomes available, we reassess the potential liability related to pending claims and litigation and may revise our estimates. Due to the inherent uncertainties of the legal and regulatory process in the multiple jurisdictions in which we operate, our judgments may be materially different than the actual outcomes. Income Taxes In calculating our effective income tax rate, estimates are required regarding the timing and amount of taxable and deductible items which will adjust the pretax income earned in various tax jurisdictions. Through our interpretation of local tax regulations, adjustments to pretax income for income earned in various tax jurisdictions are reflected within various tax filings. Although we believe that our estimates and judgments discussed herein are reasonable, actual results may be materially different than the estimated amounts. We record a valuation allowance to reduce our deferred tax assets to the amount that is more likely than not to be realized. Significant judgment is required in determining the valuation allowance. In assessing the need for a valuation allowance, we consider all sources of taxable income, including projected future taxable income, reversing taxable temporary differences and ongoing tax planning strategies. If it is determined that we are able to realize deferred tax assets in excess of the net carrying value or to the extent we are unable to realize a deferred tax asset, we would adjust the valuation allowance in the period in which such a determination is made, with a corresponding increase or decrease to earnings. We record tax liabilities for uncertain tax positions taken, or expected to be taken, which may not be sustained or may only be partially sustained, upon examination by the relevant taxing authorities. We consider all relevant facts and current authorities in the tax law in assessing whether any benefit resulting from an uncertain tax position is more likely than not to be sustained and, if so, how current law impacts the amount reflected within these financial statements. If upon examination, we realize a tax benefit which is not fully sustained or is more favorably sustained, this would generally increase earnings in the period. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: Class A Common Stock and Governance Structure Provisions in our organizational documents and Delaware law could be considered anti-takeover provisions and have an impact on change-in-control. Provisions contained in our amended and restated certificate of incorporation and bylaws and Delaware law could be considered anti-takeover provisions, including provisions that could delay or prevent entirely a merger or acquisition that our stockholders consider favorable. These provisions may also discourage acquisition proposals or have the effect of delaying or preventing entirely a change in control, which could harm our stock price. For example, subject to limited exceptions, our amended and restated certificate of incorporation prohibits any person from beneficially owning more than 15% of any of the Class A common stock or any other class or series of our stock with general voting power, or more than 15% of our total voting power. In addition: • our stockholders are not entitled to the right to cumulate votes in the election of directors • our stockholders are not entitled to act by written consent • any representative of a Mastercard or Mastercard Foundation competitor is disqualified from service on our board of directors Mastercard Foundation’s substantial stock ownership, and restrictions on its sales, may impact corporate actions or acquisition proposals favorable to, or favored by, the other public stockholders. Mastercard Foundation owns shares of our Class A common stock representing greater than 5% of our general voting power. Historically, Mastercard Foundation had been restricted from selling or otherwise transferring its shares of Class A common stock prior to May 1, 2027, except to the extent necessary to satisfy its charitable disbursement requirements, for which purpose earlier sales were permitted and had occurred. In July 2023, pursuant to an application in consultation with Mastercard, Mastercard Foundation received court approval to advance that date to January 1, 2024. As a result, Mastercard Foundation is now permitted to sell all or part of its remaining shares, subject to certain conditions. In March 2024, Mastercard Foundation began selling shares pursuant to an orderly and structured plan to diversify its Mastercard shares over a seven-year period, while committing to remain a long-term Mastercard stockholder and retaining a significant holding of Mastercard shares in its portfolio. The directors of Mastercard Foundation are required to be independent of us and our customers. The ownership of Class A common stock by Mastercard Foundation, together with the seven-year diversification plan, could discourage or make more difficult acquisition proposals favored by other holders of the Class A common stock. In addition, because Mastercard Foundation intends to sell its shares over an extended period of time, it may not have the same interest in short or medium-term movements in our stock price as, or incentive to approve a corporate action that may be favorable to, our other stockholders. credit_strengths.text: Mastercard's operating margin exceeds the sector median, reflecting the scalability of its payment network and pricing power. Revenue and operating income have grown steadily over the past three fiscal years, with operating cash flow rising in tandem. This consistent profitability supports strong internal cash generation and provides a buffer against cyclical volume declines.

Interest coverage is exceptionally high, with operating income covering gross interest expense many times over. Gross leverage sits below the sector median, and net leverage is modest after netting cash. The indicative financial risk profile is Minimal, with substantial headroom before the next leverage threshold, suggesting ample capacity to absorb moderate EBITDA declines.

key_risks.text: The debt note discloses a substantial maturity wall: scheduled principal repayments rise sharply in the third year and remain elevated thereafter, with a large tail beyond year five. Refinancing this ladder at higher rates could pressure interest costs, though current coverage provides a cushion. The floating-rate notes due in the third year add exposure to SOFR resets.

Risk factors highlight Mastercard Foundation's seven-year diversification plan and its large voting stake, which could discourage acquisition proposals and create governance overhang. Additionally, legal and tax contingencies require significant judgment, and adverse outcomes could materially affect earnings and cash flow, as noted in the MD&A.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Free cash flow covers debt many times over, and the ratio of free cash flow to debt is well above the sector median. Operating cash flow is more than double total debt, indicating robust capacity to service obligations. However, shareholder distributions absorb most free cash flow, leaving limited retained cash for debt reduction.

The current ratio is marginally above parity, consistent with the sector median, and cash balances are substantial. Yet current liabilities are largely matched by current assets, leaving little working capital cushion. The upcoming maturity within the next twelve months is manageable given cash on hand and expected cash generation.

overall_credit_view.text: Mastercard's credit profile is supported by a Minimal indicative financial risk profile, with leverage well below the sector median and interest coverage far exceeding peers. The business generates substantial free cash flow, but shareholder returns consume the bulk of it, constraining deleveraging. We view the credit as strong, with capacity to withstand moderate earnings volatility.

Forward-looking, we expect continued revenue growth and cash generation, but refinancing risk from the maturity ladder and potential legal or tax liabilities warrant monitoring. The absence of a debt-note passage would limit visibility on covenant terms, but the disclosed maturity schedule and floating-rate exposure are key considerations. Overall, we assess the credit as investment grade with a stable outlook.

credit_strengths.text: Mastercard的營運利潤率高於行業中位數，反映其支付網絡的可擴展性及定價能力。過去三個財政年度，收入及營運收入穩步增長，營運現金流亦同步上升。此持續的盈利能力支持強勁的內部現金生成，並為週期性交易量下降提供緩衝。
利息覆蓋率極高，營運收入覆蓋總利息支出多倍。總槓桿低於行業中位數，扣除現金後淨槓桿適度。指示性財務風險狀況為極低，距離下一個槓桿門檻有大量空間，顯示有充足能力吸收適度的EBITDA下降。

key_risks.text: 債務票據披露了龐大的到期牆：預定本金償還在第三年大幅上升，其後維持高位，五年後仍有大量尾部。以較高利率為此階梯再融資可能對利息成本構成壓力，儘管當前覆蓋率提供緩衝。第三年到期的浮動利率票據增加了對SOFR重設的風險敞口。
風險因素強調Mastercard Foundation的七年多元化計劃及其大量投票權持股，可能阻礙收購提案並造成治理懸而未決。此外，法律及稅務或有事項需要重大判斷，不利結果可能重大影響盈利及現金流，如MD&A所述。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 自由現金流覆蓋債務多倍，自由現金流與債務比率遠高於行業中位數。營運現金流超過總債務兩倍以上，顯示償付義務的強勁能力。然而，股東分派吸收大部分自由現金流，留下有限留存現金用於減債。
流動比率略高於一，與行業中位數一致，現金結餘龐大。然而，流動負債大致由流動資產匹配，留下少量營運資金緩衝。未來十二個月內的到期債務，鑑於手頭現金及預期現金生成，屬可管理。

overall_credit_view.text: Mastercard的信用狀況受極低的指示性財務風險狀況支持，槓桿遠低於行業中位數，利息覆蓋率遠超同業。業務產生大量自由現金流，但股東回報消耗大部分，限制去槓桿。我們認為該信用強勁，有能力承受適度的盈利波動。
前瞻性而言，我們預期收入及現金生成持續增長，但到期階梯的再融資風險及潛在法律或稅務負債值得監控。缺乏債務票據段落將限制對契約條款的能見度，但披露的到期時間表及浮動利率風險敞口是關鍵考慮因素。總體而言，我們評估該信用為投資級，展望穩定。
